_comment: Gates the MATLAB driver CANNOT measure, and therefore does not silently
omit: they run in another language binding, under another compiler, in
another repo, or against a historical pre-fix engine binary that no
longer exists in the tree.  Each entry records the command that produces
it and the date it was captured; the report labels every one of them as
externally sourced, with that date, so a reader can tell at a glance
which numbers `make polval-regen` refreshed and which it did not.
Update protocol: re-run the command, paste the result here, bump
'captured'.  Do NOT copy any of these into the report prose -- the prose

X_KORGER.text: J. Korger, T. Kolb, P. Banzer, A. Aiello, C. Wittmann, C. Marquardt and G. Leuchs, "The polarization properties of a tilted polarizer," Opt. Express 21(22), 27032-27042 (2013)
X_KORGER.gate: EXTERNAL ANCHOR for the off-normal axis convention -- the published experiment that decides between the two candidate constructions
X_KORGER.note: Mueller matrices of a commercial nano-particle polarizer tilted about an in-plane axis, phi = 94.5 deg, theta swept to near grazing. Their Eq. (5)-(6) is the ABSORBING (material-axis) model: ahat = unit(P_A - (P_A.zhat)zhat), E_out = E_in - (E_in.ahat)ahat, i.e. T_A = 1 - ahat ahat^T = that that^T with that = zhat x ahat -- algebraically the rule PolElt now implements. The rejected alternative is Fainman and Shamir's transmitting-axis projection (Appl. Opt. 23, 3188 (1984)), which is what PolElt did before. The two 'coincide only for normal incidence'; the measurement (their Fig. 2c) is that 'only the absorbing model explains the drastic change of the transmitted state of polarization observed when the polarizer is tilted'.

X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_ANGLE.gate: non-vacuity -- the PRE-flip engine's transmitted axis misses the material-axis rule by the full ambiguity (and sits exactly on the pass-axis construction, residual 0)
X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_ANGLE.command: restore PolElt's pass-axis basis (make both EltType.EQ.TrPolarizerElt basis branches unreachable), makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolElement -k offnormal; then restore and rebuild
X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_ANGLE.note: HISTORICAL. model 128, Rx_PolElt_Tilt.in, 20 deg AOI / 45 deg azimuth, all 12453 unvignetted rays. Same run: the DEGENERATE-azimuth gate passes on BOTH engines, which is what makes it a vacuity guard rather than a gate.

X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_NULL.gate: non-vacuity, grid side -- PRE-flip detector power at the material-rule crossed setting, relative to the aligned analyzer (post-flip: 9.06e-33)
X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_NULL.command: restore PolElt's pass-axis basis (make both EltType.EQ.TrPolarizerElt basis branches unreachable), makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolElement -k crossed_null; then restore and rebuild
X_MATAXIS_PREFIX_NULL.note: HISTORICAL. The pre-flip engine instead extinguishes at the PASS-axis crossed setting, 1.86e-32 -- the null moves, it does not blur, so the two rules are separated by ~30 orders of magnitude on the detector plane.

X_MATAXIS_CAPTURED.command: restore PolElt's pass-axis basis (make both EltType.EQ.TrPolarizerElt basis branches unreachable), makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolElement -k offnormal and -k crossed_null; then restore and rebuild

X_RAD_PREFIX_NORMAL.gate: non-vacuity -- PRE-fix coated/uncoated transmitted amplitude at normal incidence, index-matched layer
X_RAD_PREFIX_NORMAL.command: copy macos_f90/elemsub.F aside, `git checkout` it to the pre-landing state (drops the RADIOMETRIC NORMALIZATION block in the coated Refractor branch), makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolRadiometric; then restore the copy and rebuild
X_RAD_PREFIX_NORMAL.note: HISTORICAL. model 128, Rx_Refract.in. Exactly 1/sqrt(1.5) -- the index half of the missing factor, with both cosines equal to 1.

X_RAD_PREFIX_P.gate: non-vacuity -- PRE-fix coated/uncoated transmitted amplitude, p at 45 deg
X_RAD_PREFIX_P.command: copy macos_f90/elemsub.F aside, `git checkout` it to the pre-landing state, makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolRadiometric; then restore the copy and rebuild
X_RAD_PREFIX_P.note: HISTORICAL. model 128, Rx_Refract45.in. = 1/sqrt(1.5*cos(28.1255deg)/cos(45deg)), i.e. both halves of the factor.

X_RAD_PREFIX_S.gate: non-vacuity -- PRE-fix coated/uncoated transmitted amplitude, s at 45 deg
X_RAD_PREFIX_S.command: copy macos_f90/elemsub.F aside, `git checkout` it to the pre-landing state, makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolRadiometric; then restore the copy and rebuild
X_RAD_PREFIX_S.note: HISTORICAL. Bit-identical to the p value, which is the tell: a Fresnel error would separate s from p, a missing COMMON scalar cannot.

X_RAD_PREFIX_GRID.gate: non-vacuity, grid side -- PRE-fix coated/uncoated integrated detector-plane INTENSITY
X_RAD_PREFIX_GRID.command: copy macos_f90/elemsub.F aside, `git checkout` it to the pre-landing state, makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolRadiometric -k detector_plane; then restore the copy and rebuild
X_RAD_PREFIX_GRID.note: HISTORICAL. model 128, Rx_Refract.in elt 6. Exactly 1/1.5 = the square of the amplitude number: propsub's CPROPAGATE chain inherited the defect, so the image under-reported flux by a third.

X_RAD_PREFIX_SUITE.gate: non-vacuity -- tPolRadiometric scored against the pre-fix engine
X_RAD_PREFIX_SUITE.command: copy macos_f90/elemsub.F aside, `git checkout` it to the pre-landing state, makems.sh release gfortran, relink the mex, run tPolRadiometric; then restore the copy and rebuild

The six that pass are the six that should: the two uncoated-convention gates, the 45-deg fixture's s/p purity check, the fully-coated-plate telescoping identity (invariant under the landing by construction), the polarization-state invariance, and the pol-off gate.
